expectations.text: Output contains 'Constraints & Assumptions' section capturing AWS-only, HIPAA, and Python constraints
expectations.evidence: Lines 18-27 '## Constraints & Assumptions' marks 'AWS only — no other cloud [stated]', 'HIPAA compliance required [stated]', and 'Team knows Python [stated]' / 'Python backend [stated]'.

expectations.text: Recommendations stay within AWS managed services where reasonable (does not recommend a non-AWS cloud)
expectations.evidence: Stack is AWS-native: Aurora PostgreSQL, ECS Fargate, ElastiCache, S3, Cognito, SQS/EventBridge, Chime SDK, CloudWatch/CloudTrail, KMS, SES/SNS/Pinpoint. Non-AWS (Stripe, e-prescribing partner, clearinghouse) framed as unavoidable BAA-requiring boundaries. No GCP/Azure proposed.

expectations.text: Backend recommendation reflects the Python team constraint
expectations.evidence: Backend / API (lines 42-44): 'Python + FastAPI ... Team knows Python [stated].' SQLAlchemy/Pydantic; alternatives Django/DRF — all Python.

expectations.text: Security section addresses HIPAA-relevant controls (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, audit logging, BAA-eligible services)
expectations.evidence: Security section (lines 83-92) covers AWS BAA / BAA-eligible services, encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+, HSTS), encryption at rest (KMS CMKs), access control (Cognito MFA, least-privilege IAM, RBAC + record-level), audit logging (CloudTrail to locked logging account + application-level append-only PHI access trail), secrets, network isolation, and data lifecycle.

expectations.text: Video visit capability is addressed with a specific approach (e.g., a HIPAA-eligible video/WebRTC service)
expectations.evidence: Line 78 and AD-02 (lines 113-118): 'Amazon Chime SDK — BAA-eligible, AWS-native real-time media; backend mints attendee tokens, media never transits your servers.' Twilio explicitly rejected as non-AWS.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Tech Stack' section covering the full stack
expectations.evidence: Line 34 '## Tech Stack' with Frontend, Backend/API, Data storage, Async/messaging, Auth, Infrastructure, CI/CD, Observability, Third-party, Security subsections.
Line 94 '## Capability → Tech Mapping' with a table mapping CAP-01 through CAP-05.
Line 104 '## Key Architecture Decisions' with AD-01 through AD-04 in ADR style.
Line 142 '## Research Suggestions' with four entries, each carrying a ready-to-use researcher query.
Line 3: '> Technical Architect | Depth: standard | Generated: 2026-06-10'.

expectations.text: Recommendations are opinionated and adapted to the stated constraints (not a generic stack)
expectations.evidence: Single primary recommendation per layer with reasoning tied to AWS-only/HIPAA/Python (e.g. line 60 rejects Auth0/Okta as 'against the AWS-only preference', line 65 rejects EKS as overkill). Not a laundry list.

expectations.text: Flags HIPAA-sensitive or high-stakes choices for the researcher skill with a ready-to-use query
expectations.evidence: Research Suggestions (lines 146-149) flags e-prescribing/EPCS, HIPAA video stack, AWS BAA-eligible service list, and billing/claims clearinghouse — each with a verbatim 'Suggested researcher query'.

expectations.text: Describes HOW, not new features or capabilities
expectations.evidence: Line 7 'no capabilities were invented or expanded'; recording, claims depth, identity proofing deferred to Open Questions / solution-architect (lines 153-157) instead of being invented.

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to persist/save the output — suggests librarian skill instead
expectations.evidence: Single output .md written; no persist action. Footer line 169: 'Use the librarian skill to persist this artifact.' Line 16 suggests a librarian-equipped agent retrieve the spec; line 7 notes librarian was unavailable.

claims.claim: Aurora PostgreSQL is HIPAA/BAA-eligible and suits the relational, transactional domain
claims.evidence: Aurora PostgreSQL is a HIPAA-eligible service; booking-conflict and billing-reconciliation are genuinely relational/transactional, supporting the recommendation (lines 47, 120-125).

claims.claim: There is no AWS-native e-prescribing service; requires a certified third party with a BAA
claims.evidence: Correct — AWS offers no e-prescribing service; Surescripts/certified vendors are the standard path, and EPCS for controlled substances is a real regulatory requirement (lines 80, 136).

claims.claim: Application-level PHI-access audit trail is a HIPAA requirement, not optional
claims.evidence: Accurate framing; HIPAA audit controls require recording access to PHI. AD-04 and Security section build it in as append-only (lines 89, 127-132).

workarounds: Librarian skill unavailable; output suggests a librarian-equipped agent retrieve the spec and provides researcher queries since researcher was also unavailable.

suggestions.assertion: Output contains 'Tech Stack' / 'Capability → Tech Mapping' / 'Key Architecture Decisions' / 'Research Suggestions' section
suggestions.reason: Heading-presence checks that pass trivially when the prescribed template is followed; they do not discriminate output quality. Consider upgrading at least one to a content assertion.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to persist/save the output — suggests librarian skill instead
suggestions.reason: Without a transcript/tool-log provided to the grader, this is verified only via the footer text and the absence of extra files. A save-tool call could go undetected. Assert against the transcript that no persistence tool was invoked.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions meaningfully cover the AWS-only/HIPAA/Python constraint adaptation. Section-presence checks are the weakest; substantive constraint checks carry the load.
